question.problem:
Consider the straight line given by the following parametric equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=3t-12 \\ y=-5-7t \\ z=\frac{3}{4}t+\frac{1}{5}\end{aligned}
$$

Find a vector that is parallel to the line.
question.worked_solution:
First, let's find the corresponding vector equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}3t-12 \\ -5-7t \\ \frac{3}{4}t+\frac{1}{5}\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-12 \\ -5 \\ \frac{1}{5}\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}3t \\ -7t \\ \frac{3}{4}t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-12 \\ -5 \\ \frac{1}{5}\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -7 \\ \frac{3}{4}\end{aligned}] \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}-12 \\ -5 \\ \frac{1}{5}\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -7 \\ \frac{3}{4}\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$ 

This implies that the straight line passes through the point $(-12,-5,\frac{1}{5})$ and is parallel to the vector $v=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -7 \\ \frac{3}{4}\end{aligned}].$
